description: Two storey front extension incorporating porch; Single storey side extension; Conversion of garage to habitable room; Alterations to roof to raise ridge height and form rear dormers; External alterations
decision_conditions: The proposed development would result in a substantial cumulative enlargement of the original and existing dwelling, the scale of which&nbsp;represents a disproportionate addition over and above the size of the original building and therefore constitutes inappropriate and disproportionate development within the Green Belt, as defined by the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).&nbsp;No very special circumstances have been demonstrated to outweigh this harm.&nbsp;The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024),&nbsp;Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy GI1 of Harrow's New Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;

<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;"><span style="line-height:115%"><span style="line-height: 115%;">The proposed development would fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Conservation Area. The infilling between the house and garage would erode the characteristic spacing and create an awkward, bulky form contrary to the Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Strategy (CAAMS). The two‑storey front extension, including the porch and associated architectural features, would form an overly dominant and formal addition that disrupts the restrained neo‑classical character of the original dwelling, contrary to CAAMS guidance on visually intrusive entrance features. The increased roof ridge height would result in excessive bulk and an incongruous roof form harmful to the established roofscape, conflicting with CAAMS guidance on the sensitivity of roofs within the Conservation Area. As such, the proposal would cause harm to the significance of the Conservation Area, contrary to Section 72 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 and relevant local plan policies and would be contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), policies GR1 and&nbsp;HE1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041),&nbsp;the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010) and adopted the </span></span>Pinner Conservation Areas SPD Appendix 9 the Pinner Hill Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Strategy<span style="line-height:115%"><span style="line-height: 115%;">(2009).</span></span></p>
